fields.description:
## Context / Problem

The sibling selector writes a labeled candidate manifest — per criterion, the candidates
with their direction, tier, supporting signals and rank. Nothing yet turns that into files
the eval runner can consume, and the file format is not free-form: `validate_eval_spec` under
`strict=True` rejects a spec that lacks an explicit `epochs`, a satisfiable `at_least(k)`
gate, a `coverage_threshold` in [0, 1], a non-empty `scorers` list holding at least one
registered deterministic scorer, a balanced dataset, or a non-empty `gold_set` whose entries
each carry an `input` and a `label` (`eval.py:252-272`, `eval.py:288-300`). Each dataset case
must also carry a payload field (`input`/`plan`/`finding`/`spec`) beyond the metadata keys
(`eval.py:249-250`).

Two of those constraints cannot be satisfied by transcription alone. A criterion may yield
candidates on only one side of the fire/no-fire axis, which fails the balance rule at
`eval.py:252-255`; and a stale file from an earlier run would survive for a criterion that
has since become skipped, silently keeping a retired assertion in the suite.

## Approach

An emitter that reads the manifest and writes one `.eval.yaml` per criterion into a working
directory for the sibling admission runner. It issues no model call and reads NOTHING beyond
the manifest — it is a pure, deterministic function of the manifest rows.

**Manifest is the sole input; case payloads are DERIVED, not transcribed.** The selector's
candidate row (`fixture_selection.py:33-38`) carries only `criterion`, `direction`, `norm_id`,
`tier`, `rank`, `signals`, `escaped_defect`, `abs_margin`, `review_event_uuid` — it holds no
plan prose, no `expect`, no `corpus`, no case `id`, and no gold material. The emitter therefore
deterministically derives (synthesizes) every emitted field from those recorded row fields, by a fixed rule and
with no model call:

- `expect` (dataset) and `label` (gold_set) come from the candidate's recorded `direction`:
  a `fire` candidate maps to `expect: finding` / `label: finding`, a `no_fire` candidate maps
  to `expect: pass` / `label: pass`. This is the only fire/no-fire → validator-axis mapping.
- `id` is `<prompt_id>-<direction>-<rank>`, where `prompt_id` is
  `criteria.ids.criterion_prompt_id(criterion)` and `rank` is the row's recorded rank; this is
  unique within a spec because fire and no_fire ranks are namespaced by direction.
- `corpus` is the constant `rebar` (the committed review corpus the manifest was mined from);
  `criterion` is the row's `criterion`.
- `input` is a DETERMINISTIC, model-free textual descriptor rendered from the row's stable
  fields — its `criterion`, `direction`, `tier`, sorted `signals`, and its `norm_id` (fire) or
  `review_event_uuid` (no_fire) and `rank`. It is a compact provenance string, NOT authored
  plan prose and NOT resolved from any external store; its sole jobs are to satisfy the
  validator's required payload field and to give the gold entry a stable, unique reference.
- `gold_set` is exactly one `{input, label}` entry per emitted dataset case (same synthesized
  `input`, `label` = the case's `expect`), so gold material exists for a criterion precisely
  when that criterion contributes dataset cases.

**Emitted spec fields.** Each file carries exactly the field set of the committed
`.rebar/evals/plan-review-project-portability.eval.yaml`: `prompt` (the criterion's prompt
id via `criterion_prompt_id`), `model`, `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`,
`coverage_threshold: 1.0`, a `scorers` list holding the registered deterministic scorer
`emits_valid_findings` from `eval_scorers`, a `dataset` of `{id, corpus, criterion, expect,
input}` cases, and a `gold_set` of `{input, label}` entries. `epochs: 3` with `at_least(2)`
matches the convention every shipped spec already uses, so the emitted files need no second
standard.

**Case selection.** At most 8 cases per criterion, at most 4 per side, taken in the manifest's
recorded rank order so the output is a deterministic function of the manifest.

**Balance guarantee.** A criterion that cannot supply at least one candidate row on EACH side
of the fire/no-fire axis emits NO file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced` in the emitter's
report. Because both the dataset cases and their gold entries derive from the same candidate
rows, a one-sided criterion — and equally a criterion present only as a `zero_candidate` row,
which contributes no candidate on either side — yields no balanced dataset and no gold
material, so it never reaches the validator. The sibling self-healing loop counts
`skipped-unbalanced` as a failed attempt, so a persistently unbalanced criterion is recorded
by that child's `unreliable-criterion:` breaker rather than vanishing silently.

**Output lifecycle.** Each run writes a fresh temporary tree and atomically replaces the
working directory, so no file survives for a criterion that has become skipped or that
already has a spec.

## Scope

The emitter module under `src/rebar/llm/evals/`, its YAML serialization, the deterministic
per-field derivation above, the per-side case selection, the balance refusal and the emitter
report. It reads the manifest produced by the sibling selector and writes only into its own
working directory.

## Non-goals

- Deciding which candidates qualify, their tier, or their rank; the selector owns all of that
  and this child transcribes its recorded order.
- Writing into `.rebar/evals/` or admitting a spec; the admission runner owns both.
- Any model call, or any read of the ticket store, git, or the review corpus; the manifest is
  the sole input.
- Emitting for a criterion that already has a spec, since `eval.py:69-78` resolves a project
  spec as a replacement and a mined file would delete the packaged cases.

## Testing

Unit tests over the serializer and the balance refusal using synthetic manifests, invoking
the real `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)` on every emitted file rather than asserting
on YAML text. Every assertion is deterministic because no model is involved.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Every emitted spec returns zero errors from `validate_eval_spec(spec, strict=True)`;
      verified by `pytest` invoking the real validator over each emitted file.
- [ ] An emitted spec carries `epochs: 3`, `gate: at_least(2)`, `coverage_threshold: 1.0` and
      a `scorers` entry naming `emits_valid_findings`; verified by `pytest` asserting those
      four values on a spec built from a synthetic manifest.
- [ ] Each dataset case's `expect` is `finding` for a `fire` candidate and `pass` for a
      `no_fire` candidate, and each gold_set entry's `label` equals its case's `expect`;
      verified by `pytest` asserting the mapping on a spec built from a mixed-direction
      manifest.
- [ ] A criterion whose manifest holds candidates on only one side emits no file and is
      counted `skipped-unbalanced`; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent and the
      report names the criterion.
- [ ] A criterion present in the manifest with no candidate row on either side (for example,
      only a `zero_candidate` row) emits no file and is counted `skipped-unbalanced`; verified
      by `pytest` asserting the path is absent and the report names the criterion.
- [ ] Given a manifest with 6 ranked candidates on one side and at least one on the other, the
      emitted dataset holds the first 4 of the six in rank order; verified by `pytest`
      asserting the emitted case ids and order.
- [ ] A file written by a previous run for a criterion absent from the current manifest does
      not survive the next run; verified by `pytest` asserting the path is absent after the
      second run.
- [ ] Two consecutive runs over the same manifest emit byte-identical output; verified by
      `diff -r` of the two output trees exiting 0.
- [ ] The emitter completes with the repository's network guard active; verified by `pytest`
      running it under that guard.

## Definition of Done

`make lint`, `make typecheck` and `make test` pass; a run over the real manifest emits specs
that all pass the strict validator; the diff touches nothing under `.rebar/evals/` or
`src/rebar/llm/reviewers/`.

## Budget

**$0.** Emission is a pure, model-free function of the manifest.
